gap: No result ChatGPT got states that none of these kits can charge from their panels when the battery is below freezing: the makers set the charging floor at 32°F (0°C) even though discharging is allowed down to −4°F, and none of the stations has a battery heater. So in a winter outage, a station left outside next to its panels takes in nothing until it is brought somewhere warmer.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts (cited) and wearesalt.org. StormWatts already covers the other wiring check: the panels' voltage on a cold morning, series versus parallel, and the station's input current limit for the Elite 200 V2 and EcoFlow kits. That half of the finding is not new (0). Neither StormWatts nor wearesalt gives a charging-temperature floor or says that no station has a battery heater. wearesalt only says the Elite 200 V2's 60 V cap makes its 1,000 W solar maximum hard to reach. I could not open our own two pages, theoutageready.com or solargenreview.com (certificate errors and HTTP 429), so I can't say whether those pages mention the floor.
decides: It doesn't change which kit wins, because every candidate stops charging at 32°F. It does change how the kit gets used. In November, the plan only works if the station stays indoors or somewhere above freezing while the panels sit outside on an MC4 extension. That makes the extension cable a needed add-on in winter and makes the cold-weather Voc check apply to the panels, not the station. The pick still turns on price and shipping state. One issue for the pick: ALLPOWERS lists the R3500 on its own as sold out and the SP037 panel as a pre-order dispatching Nov 20, 2026. The 'ships now' status our table gives the R3500 + SP037 kit needs a fresh check before that kit is named as the ships-now pick.

findings.label: Charging vs discharging temperature range (maker's words)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI blog: What happens to batteries in extreme cold (dated Nov 12, 2026)
findings.note: BLUETTI: 'At 23°F (−5°C), that temperature is within its discharge interval but below its charging minimum' and 'the discharge rating is not permission to charge it cold.' The page gives no range for any other BLUETTI model.

findings.label: Charging floor by model and battery heaters (named reviewer)
findings.value: Charging range: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 32–104°F; Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 32–113°F; EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max 32–113°F; Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 32–104°F. None of the 21 models checked has a built-in battery heater.
findings.source_title: Backup Power Hub (Dan Miller, Oct 8, 2026): Freeze warnings are here: never charge a power station below 32°F, and what each brand's manual says
findings.note: Backup Power Hub says it read the US manuals and product pages but links none. It says the battery management system blocks charging below freezing on every current EcoFlow, Jackery, Anker and BLUETTI model. Jackery's heated Extreme Guard bag for the 2000 v2 is an external accessory, not a heater. ALLPOWERS, the Elite 300/400 and the Apex 200 are not covered.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2*200W Solar (BLUETTI US store)
findings.note: Quoted from the page FAQ: 'PV input: Elite 200 V2: 12V-60V/20A, 1,000W max'. The store lists the kit at $1,499.00, available. The kit's URL shows the panels are SP200L. Ship dates on the page: base unit 'Pre-order: Ships from 11.26', 200 W panel 'ships from 11.18'. No temperature specs on this page or on the bare-unit page.

findings.label: Series wiring check (rival coverage)
findings.value: About 49 V in series, about 56.5 V at −4°F, inside the 12–60 V input. In parallel, about 21.6 A Isc on the 20 A input.
findings.source_title: StormWatts: Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts
findings.note: StormWatts's figures, using its own assumed −0.33%/°C coefficient. Included to show this wiring check is already on a cited rival, so it is not our gap.

findings.label: Solar input and what's in the box
findings.value: 2,000 W max, XT60, 12–150 V MPPT, 40 A; bare unit ships without a solar cable
findings.source_title: ALLPOWERS R3500 Home Backup Power Station | 3200W 3168Wh (ALLPOWERS US store)
findings.note: One single-panel SP037 is well inside 12–150 V, so wiring is not a concern for this kit. The same page shows the bare R3500 as 'Sold out / OUT OF STOCK' at $1,199 (compare-at $2,099). It lists add-ons as pre-orders: SP037 400 W 'Estimated dispatch from Nov 20, 2026', SP039 600 W 'from Nov 23, 2026'. The page gives no charging temperature.
